module_mood_contract: anticipation toward grounded competence — student leaves the lecture thinking 'I know what to look for'; the exercise earns 'I can feel when a plan is good before approving it'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Meta-frame lectures are closers, not openers; conceptual vocabulary belongs mid-module and ceiling demos may open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a primer-before-exercise lecture that introduces plan-review vocabulary (five qualities, three pressures, paired reads) and shows the calibration ceiling. It does not retrospectively name a pattern the student already lived, so the closer-only constraint does not bind. Its placement immediately before the M2 plan exercise is the rule's intended vocabulary/ceiling shape.

M2 targets grounded competence, not the M4/M5-style contrast mood in which explanation would pre-empt felt evidence. This lecture is explicitly the M2 vocabulary primer, while the exercise still owns the felt payoff.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The teaching slides contain no forward or backward module sequencing. The line-3 session label names the current session ('Module 2 - Plan mode done right') as setup metadata; it is not a bridge or a claim about another module.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide and lecture headers pass the squint test and truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All eight headers name their payload cold and at the strength the body supports: tool/instruction change, optional direct inspection, five qualities, three pressures, paired reads, find-versus-judge, plan review as gate, and the complexity ceiling. The revised paired-read body now explicitly qualifies the walk-down as optional and supplies a stop condition, so its header remains true without claiming both reads are mandatory in every case.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide body is size-bounded: under about 210 readable words and no more than six bullets.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/when-a-plan-is-good.md` reports 8 slides, 0 oversized. The revised paired-read slide remains below both limits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, with optional refinements allowed in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The only action on this lecture's page is an explicitly optional registered prompt. The revised body does not replace the later exercise's full-on walk-down prompt; it gives the professional student the decision rule around that optional refinement: human push-back first, continue while answers materially sharpen the plan, and stop when they do not. This is the rule's optional-refinement carve-out, not leaked session machinery or a scripted count.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom is the default delivery; body teaches work and the trainer manages the room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No body sentence authors a pair, group, room-share, pause, or trainer cue. Every instruction concerns the student's session, plan read, judgment, or next action; room pacing stays outside the lecture body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; the 8+ floor applies to teaching beats.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The regenerated single-persona trace scores the whole teaching phase 8/10 and the close 8/10. The session rename is setup inside that phase and mood-exempt; the teaching body itself produces anticipation toward grounded competence without trainer compensation: 'I know what to look for,' with the felt proof reserved for the exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Epistemic mood is not punitive mood.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The lecture frames uncertainty as what the plan has not yet decided and what the engineer can surface, never as a student mistake. The revised stopping rule reduces performance pressure: deeper questioning is useful only while it materially sharpens the plan.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The title and headers lead with positive disciplines: knowing when a plan is good, paired reads, judgment, plan review, calibration, and checks. Persuasive but weak plans appear as contrast cases inside the discipline rather than as the lecture's governing frame.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy fidelity consolidates Big Idea, front-run, arc handoff, and mood-does-not-resolve-early checks.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea fidelity: the lecture treats plan mode as a review discipline and cheap calibration gate, not a feature tour. Front-run: it does not execute the plan, name plan-mode approval inflation before the exercise retro, or expose Pocock's move as a Skill before M3. The full walk-down remains available in the later copied prompt; the new stop rule governs whether continuing is valuable, not whether the plan itself gets read. Arc handoff: the student leaves with the exact five-qualities/three-pressures/two-read vocabulary the M2 exercise turns into action. Mood timing: the lecture stops at 'I know what to look for' and does not claim the exercise's felt grounded competence in advance.
